description: We are Team CrewPULSE, an interdisciplinary team building a human-centered crew health and mission risk intelligence platform for space exploration. Our vision is to help protect astronaut wellbeing, cognitive performance, and mission readiness through evidence-based data analysis, AI-assisted insights, and NASA human systems research. We welcome passionate innovators who want to contribute to aerospace, AI, software engineering, biomedical systems, and space exploration.
summary:
CrewPULSEx is a human-centered crew health and mission risk intelligence platform designed to support astronaut well-being and safer long-duration space missions. The platform provides an integrated environment for crew management, mission monitoring, health-related risk assessment, and operational intelligence.

By combining structured crew information, evidence-based data analysis, rule-based risk forecasting, and mission management tools, CrewPULSEx helps mission teams organize critical information and identify potential concerns that could affect crew performance and mission success.

Developed with modern web technologies and a cloud-connected backend, the platform demonstrates how digital health intelligence and human-systems research can contribute to safer, more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
CrewPULSEx — Intelligent Crew Health and Mission Risk Intelligence Platform

CrewPULSEx is a human-centered crew health and mission-support platform designed to help mission teams organize crew information, monitor simulated health and performance indicators, and identify potential risks that could affect astronaut well-being and mission readiness.

The platform provides role-based access, crew management, mission dashboards, risk indicators, and mission intelligence features. Its risk insights use rule-based logic and simulated demonstration data to help users recognize potential concerns and understand how crew health, performance, and mission conditions can be considered together.

The project addresses an important challenge in human space exploration: maintaining crew health and performance during demanding missions, particularly those involving isolation, confinement, altered gravity, radiation exposure, and long communication distances. By bringing crew information and risk-related insights into one interface, CrewPULSEx aims to support clearer situational awareness, better-informed decisions, and more organized mission support.

The project draws on NASA Human System Risk Board research and publications concerning behavioral health risks, human-system risk management, causal diagramming, and levels of evidence. These resources informed the project's research direction and conceptual approach. CrewPULSEx is an independent prototype; it does not reproduce official NASA risk assessments, claim NASA endorsement, or provide clinically validated predictions.

The platform was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express.js, and Supabase PostgreSQL. It includes a web frontend, backend API, database connectivity, and role-based application workflows. The frontend is deployed on Vercel, while the backend is hosted on Render.

The project's creativity lies in combining crew management, mission awareness, and risk-oriented insights into a single spaceflight-focused interface. The design considers usability, clarity, crew well-being, mission constraints, data privacy, and the importance of distinguishing simulated indicators from validated medical information.

The intended impact is to demonstrate how an integrated digital platform could help future mission teams organize crew information and consider human-system risks. Future development could include validated assessment methods, secure wearable-sensor integration, live telemetry, richer evidence-based analytics, and expanded multi-crew monitoring. These capabilities are proposed future enhancements and are not claimed as implemented features.
